property_summary: Only calls to withdraw made by the contract's Owner succeed (do not revert); calls by non-owners revert.
The invocation of C.Command(caller, data) should revert exactly when caller is not c.Owner() (i.e., reverted == (caller != c.Owner())).
The call to c.Command(caller, data) reverts exactly when caller is not c.Owner() (i.e., reverted == (caller != c.Owner())).
The Command invocation should revert exactly when the provided caller is not c.Owner() (i.e., reverted == (caller != c.Owner())).

For all callers and inputs, calling Command(...) must not change which caller can withdraw (Owner remains the only one able to cause the contract balance to be sent to Owner via withdraw); the mutant that removes the require in withdraw allows any caller to trigger withdraw() (draining funds to Owner) whereas the reference prevents non-Owner callers from executing withdraw, so invoking Command with a malicious callee that re-enters or causes withdraw to be executed by someone else will reveal the mutant but not the reference.

Invariant: Only the Owner address can cause the contract balance to be transferred out via withdraw() (i.e., calling withdraw() succeeds only when msg.sender == Owner); the mutant that removes the require allows any caller to trigger a successful withdraw() and thus can change address(c).balance behavior after an external Command invocation with a malicious callee that calls c.withdraw(), which violates the invariant for some fuzzed caller/amount inputs.

For all callers and Ether amounts sent into Command, only Owner can cause the contract balance to be drained via withdraw() (i.e., after calling Command with any callee behavior the contract balance remains non-negative and cannot be externally drained by a non-Owner); the mutant removing the withdraw require lets a non-Owner trigger withdraw (via a malicious callee that calls c.withdraw()) and thus can make address(c).balance drop to 0 for some fuzzed caller/amount.

For every caller and amount sent to Command, only the contract Owner can cause the contract balance to be drained via withdraw(); the mutant (removed require) allows a non-Owner to trigger withdraw (e.g., via a malicious callee that calls back into withdraw) and thus can drain the balance for some inputs.

For all callers and amounts, only the contract Owner can cause withdraw() to succeed (i.e., a non-Owner cannot make the contract transfer its balance out via withdraw); the mutant removing the require allows some non-Owner sequence (via Command interacting with a malicious callee) to trigger a successful withdraw and thus changes address(c).balance.
After calling withdraw from this test contract, the contract C's balance remains 0 (i.e., withdraw can only transfer out funds when called by the Owner).
Only the owner can successfully call withdraw (non-owner calls must revert).
Calling withdraw from this test contract must revert (i.e., the call does not succeed).
The call to c.withdraw initiated by this test must revert (i.e., reverted == true).
Non-owner calls to c.withdraw from this test contract must revert (i.e., the attempt to call withdraw should fail for this contract).

For all callers and ether sent via Command, only the Owner can successfully withdraw the contract balance (so calling withdraw by the Owner transfers out the balance); the mutant flips the require to forbid Owner, so there exist inputs where Owner can no longer withdraw (the assertion will fail for the mutant).

For every admissible input, the contract allows the Owner to successfully call withdraw() (so after funding via Command, Owner's withdraw transfers out the balance); the mutant flips the require to forbid Owner, so there exist inputs where Owner's withdraw will fail and the property is violated.

For any caller address A and any nonzero deposit amount v sent through Command to a callee that forwards (succeeds) the payment, the contract balance can always be drained by Owner via withdraw() (i.e., after funding the contract via Command, calling withdraw() as Owner succeeds); the mutant that forbids Owner from calling withdraw breaks this by making Owner's withdraw revert for some inputs.

For every caller A and any nonzero value v sent through Command to an arbitrary callee that MAY REVERT, the reference C never prevents Owner from calling withdraw() when the callee reverts (i.e., Owner can always call withdraw() without being blocked by a reverted external call), whereas the mutant that flips the access control on withdraw (require(msg.sender != Owner)) makes Owner's withdraw() revert for at least some inputs (Owner calling withdraw is rejected).

For all callers and values sent through Command to an arbitrary callee that succeeds, the contract's Owner can always call withdraw() (so a withdraw call by Owner does not revert); the mutant that flips the require to require(msg.sender != Owner) will cause Owner's withdraw() to revert for some inputs, violating this rule.

After sending some positive ETH to c and then calling withdraw, the owner (c.Owner()) receives the contract balance (address(c).balance becomes 0 and the owner balance increases by at least the withdrawn amount).
After calling multiplicate then withdraw, the owner's balance increases by at least the contract's balance immediately after the send (ownerAfter >= ownerBefore + contractAfterSend).
After sending ETH to c and then calling withdraw, the owner's balance increases by at least the contract's balance immediately after the send (ownerAfter >= ownerBefore + contractAfterSend).

After calling multiplicate (sending sendAmount) and then withdraw, the owner's balance increases by at least the contract's balance immediately after the send (ownerAfter >= ownerBefore + contractAfterSend).

After calling multiplicate (sending sendAmount) and then withdraw, the owner's balance increases by at least the contract's balance immediately after the send (ownerAfter >= ownerBefore + contractAfterSend).

For any call to Command that forwards Ether to an external callee which reverts, the correct contract C will still allow Owner to withdraw the full contract balance afterwards (i.e. withdraw succeeds and drains balance), whereas the buggy mutant requiring address(this).balance > 0 can be left unable to withdraw if the revert caused the contract balance to be zero at that moment (the mutant blocks a zero-balance transfer path and thus behaves differently for some inputs).

For any caller and any calldata/ether forwarded via Command, the reference contract C always allows the Owner to call withdraw() (i.e., withdraw() succeeds and transfers the contract balance to Owner), whereas the mutant that adds require(address(this).balance > 0) can be prevented from succeeding for some inputs where Command causes the contract balance to become zero before withdraw is called.

For any caller and any calldata/value forwarded through Command, the reference contract C always allows the Owner to successfully call withdraw() and drain address(c).balance (possibly zero) afterwards; the mutant that requires address(this).balance > 0 before transfer prevents withdraw() from succeeding when the contract balance is exactly zero, so there exist inputs (that make balance zero) where the mutant rejects withdraw() while the reference allows it.

For every input where Owner calls withdraw after any sequence driven via Command, the reference contract allows Owner to call withdraw (withdraw call does not revert) even when balance is zero; the mutant that adds require(address(this).balance > 0) will revert when balance is exactly zero, so there exist inputs (that make balance zero) where the mutant rejects withdraw while the reference permits it.

For any fuzzed caller address and fuzzed ether amount forwarded through Command to a callee that self-destructs (reducing contract balance to 0), the reference C always allows the Owner to successfully call withdraw() (withdraw does not revert and address(c).balance becomes 0 afterwards), whereas the mutant that requires address(this).balance > 0 before transfer will revert on withdraw when balance is exactly zero; the test constructs such a self-destructing callee so the mutant fails while the reference still succeeds.

For every caller and contract balance, calling withdraw() sends the entire contract balance to the Owner (so address(c).balance becomes 0 and Owner's balance increases); the mutant instead sends to msg.sender, so for some caller (an EOA different from Owner) the contract balance will not be transferred to Owner and address(c).balance won't be 0 after the call.

For every caller and any contract balance, when Owner calls withdraw() the contract balance is transferred to Owner so address(c).balance == 0 after the call; the mutant sending to msg.sender breaks this when Owner is replaced by a malicious contract that accepts ETH but does not forward it back (so address(c).balance != 0).

For every caller and starting contract balance, when the Owner calls withdraw() the contract's balance becomes zero (all funds are transferred to Owner); the mutant that transfers to msg.sender breaks this because if Owner is a contract that accepts ETH but does not forward it back (keeps it), address(c).balance will be non-zero after withdraw.

For any caller and any starting contract balance, when the Owner calls withdraw() the contract's balance becomes zero (all funds are transferred to Owner); the mutant that transfers to msg.sender can leave the contract balance non-zero when Owner != msg.sender, so this rule is violated for some inputs.

For every admissible Owner and deposit amount, when Owner calls withdraw the contract balance becomes zero (all funds are transferred to Owner); the mutant that sends to msg.sender can leave the contract balance non-zero when msg.sender != Owner.

For any caller funded as Owner and any contract balance, calling withdraw() by Owner always empties the contract (address(c).balance == 0) in the reference; the mutant that transfers a fixed 1 wei can leave non-zero balance for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller who is Owner and any positive contract balance, calling withdraw() always sends the entire contract balance to Owner (leaving address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that transfers a fixed 1 wei can leave a nonzero balance for some inputs, breaking this rule.

For any owner caller and any non-negative deposited balance, calling withdraw() empties the contract (address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that always transfers 1 wei can leave a non-zero balance for some inputs.

For any Owner caller and any prior positive contract balance, calling withdraw() results in Owner receiving at least as much Ether as the contract balance prior to the call (i.e., the reference forwards the full balance; the mutant sometimes only sends 1 wei and thus can send strictly less).

For any owner caller and any contract balance B >= 1 wei, after owner calls withdraw() the contract balance becomes 0 (reference forwards full balance); the mutant that always transfers 1 wei can leave balance > 0 for some inputs.

For any caller and any value sent, only the contract Owner can successfully call withdraw (so calls from non-Owner either revert or do not transfer funds out); the mutant that does the transfer before the require can transfer out funds even when the caller is not Owner if the transfer to Owner succeeds before the require reverts, changing the contract balance/behavior for some inputs.
